results.title: Saudi Arabia says Houthi drone intercepted near Mecca; Houthis deny targeting holy city
results.description: Saudi Arabia has warned Yemen’s Houthi group against attacks near the holy city of Mecca after its air defences intercepted and destroyed a drone south of the city on Tuesday. The Saudi-led military coalition said the drone was brought down before it could enter prohibited airspace over Mecca. Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Malki said the security of Islam’s two holiest sites and pilgrims was a “red line”, warning that necessary deterrent measures would be taken against the Houthis. Mecca is Islam’s holiest city and home to sites visited by millions of Muslims during the annual Hajj pilgrimage. Al-Malki described the incident as the second alleged Houthi attempt to target Mecca, following what the coalition said was a ballistic missile launch towards the city in July 2017. The Houthis, however, rejected the Saudi claim. Houthi spokesperson Hazem al-Assad said on social media that allegations of targeting Mecca were a repeated claim that “no longer fools anyone”. The Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) condemned what it described as an attack targeting Islam’s holy city and blamed the Houthis. The 57-member grouping also denounced what it called continued aggression against Saudi Arabia. Saudi authorities issued security alerts across several parts of the kingdom on Tuesday, including Mecca, amid a series of attacks by Iran-aligned fighters that have increased tensions in the region. The US Embassy subsequently advised Americans to reconsider travel to Saudi Arabia, citing risks including drone and missile attacks, armed conflict and terrorism. It also warned against travel to areas near the Yemen border. The latest incident comes as the Houthis have expanded their operations around the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a key global shipping route. The group has claimed several attacks against Saudi targets in recent days, including a strike on an airbase on Monday, which it said was retaliation for Saudi-led airstrikes in Yemen.

results.title: Pakistan calls for de-escalation, dialogue to resolve Yemen crisis
results.description: Amid rising violence in Yemen, Pakistan on Tuesday called for de-escalation and renewed dialogue during an emergency UN Security Council meeting — its second in less than a week — following the Houthi forces’ capture of several Red Sea islands. “The expansion of Houthi attacks in and around Bab El Mandab, this vital maritime corridor, represents a serious escalation,” Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, Pakistan’s permanent representative to the UN, told the 15-member Council. “Combined with continued violations of international law against commercial shipping, these developments pose a growing threat to freedom of navigation and the uninterrupted flow of international maritime commerce,” he said. He warned that any attempt to threaten, obstruct or weaponise the vital waterway would have consequences for international trade and commercial shipping, global supply chains and energy security. Yemen has been mired in conflict since 2014, when Houthi forces seized Sanaa, triggering a war with the internationally recognised Yemeni government. A UN-brokered truce took effect in 2022. “The relative calm painstakingly maintained in Yemen since 2022 has unfortunately collapsed,” Ambassador Asim Ahmad said. “Continued escalation risks reigniting a full-scale conflict and drawing Yemen deeper into the wider regional confrontation. This must be prevented.” At least 125,000 people have been displaced since the start of September, while the escalation threatens a critical international maritime route and has spread beyond Yemen, with Houthi attacks also reaching Saudi Arabia. Pakistan has condemned all Houthi attacks against the kingdom, underscoring that they threaten regional peace and stability, with serious consequences for the global economy and energy security. Ambassador Asim Ahmad told the Security Council that Pakistan would continue its efforts at the highest levels to help defuse tensions and advance peace and stability in the region. Reaffirming Pakistan’s unwavering support for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, security and prosperity of Saudi Arabia, he said: “Pakistan fully supports the kingdom’s legitimate right to take all necessary measures to defend its territory, protect its citizens and safeguard its national assets against any threat.” The Pakistani envoy said the current developments were exacerbating the already dire humanitarian situation in Yemen and compounding the suffering of its people, adding that diplomacy must assume urgency in proportion to the gravity of the situation. “We strongly support the resumption of an inclusive, Yemeni-led and Yemeni-owned political process under United Nations auspices,” Ambassador Asim Ahmad said. Pakistan, he said, would support all efforts to promote de-escalation, dialogue and a comprehensive political settlement that could bring lasting peace and stability to Yemen and the wider region.
